text:
Anya: Heads up — noticed dashboards undercounting last 48h on sessions and avg_latency. Looks like late telemetry is landing in Kafka but our parquet writer skipped a few partitions. Can we discuss a safe backfill?
Mike: ugh. saw spikes in kafka consumer lag around 2026-03-16 04:00 UTC. Probably the connector flapped. Do we have a list of affected date/hour partitions?
Rob: I pulled the parquet manifest and there's a gap: s3://telemetry/processed/day=2026-03-15/hour=03..05 missing. Downstream agreggates use daily partitions so daily numbers are off.
Anya: Confirmed. The aggregator job ran but there were no input files so it emitted zeros. We need to recompute for 2026-03-15 and 2026-03-16.
Jess: Two approaches: 1) re-run full DAG for those days (cleaner), 2) incremental reprocess just the missing parquet inputs and re-run the agg table for those days (cheaper). What are constraints?
Sanjay: We should avoid touching older days. Incremental is safer. We can replace parquet files for the missing hours and then run the materialized view refresh for day partitions.
Mike: How long does a materialized refresh take? Last week a full daily rebuild was ~25m with 8 workers. For 2 days expect ~50m, plus time to regenerate parquet inputs.
telemetry-bot: job-9813 (parquet-writer) FAILED at 2026-03-16T04:12:09Z — connector disconnect. Error: PartitionCommitTimeout
Rob: I can re-run the parquet-writer consumer for the 03..05 hour range in replay mode. It will produce parquet files without reprocessing downstream. Command: 
```
# replay consumer for partitions and hours
./bin/consumer-replay --topic telemetry.raw --start 2026-03-15T03:00Z --end 2026-03-15T06:00Z --output s3://telemetry/processed/day=2026-03-15/
```
Anya: Nice. After that we need an idempotent agg job. Our aggregator SQL uses insert overwrite partition which is safe. Example: 
```
INSERT OVERWRITE TABLE telemetry_daily PARTITION(day)
SELECT day, service, count(*) as sessions, avg(latency_ms) as avg_latency
FROM telemetry_parquet
WHERE day = '2026-03-15'
GROUP BY day, service;
```
Jess: For safety: run on staging with the same inputs first, then schedule production run in a canary window (single service), compare metrics diff, then full.
Sanjay: Also add a quick checksum: compare row counts between parquet input and aggregator input after replay. Rx: 
```
SELECT count(*) FROM telemetry_parquet WHERE day='2026-03-15';
SELECT sum(sessions) FROM telemetry_daily WHERE day='2026-03-15';
```
Mike: Resource question: replay will spin up consumer cluster. If we use on-demand c5.4xlarge cluster for 2 hours estimate cost ~ $12. Agg refresh with 8 workers on our analytics pool ~ $8. Total under $25. Confirm?
Rob: Should be < $30. I'll cap concurrency and throttle reads to not impact prod S3. Also add job tag/backfill-20260315.
Anya: Timeline: Rob replays now to produce parquets (ETA 30m). Jess will run staged agg (ETA 15m). If checks good, run prod agg at 02:00 UTC.
telemetry-bot: job-9814 (consumer-replay) STARTED at 2026-03-16T12:05:03Z — resources: cluster-backfill-7
Jess: Quick note — our dashboard caching TTL is 1h so some dashboards might still show stale until cache expires after we refresh the agg. We should invalidate cache keys for the affected routes.
Anya: I'll trigger cache purge after prod agg. Cache purge command: `POST https://console/api/cache/purge` body: {"paths": ["/dashboards/sessions", "/dashboards/latency"]} (will do as part of runbook)
Mike: Any risk of double-counting if parquet replay overlaps existing files? Make sure replay writes to tmp path then atomically moves into partition. Rob?
Rob: Yep — replay writes to staging and uses S3 atomic rename (put to _tmp then move). It refuses to overwrite existing files unless flag --force. I'm not using --force.
Sanjay: Good. Also add an alert rule to detect zero-row aggregates in future: if daily_sessions < 100 and previous day > 1000 then alert. I'll open a quick PR.
Anya: Ok green. Rob says replay finished and files landed. We'll run staging agg now and post diffs.
telemetry-bot: job-9814 (consumer-replay) SUCCEEDED at 2026-03-16T12:32:17Z — output: 18 parquet files written
Jess: Staging agg done. Diff: sessions +12.3% on web-service, avg_latency +4ms. Looks consistent.
Anya: Proceeding to schedule prod agg at 02:00 UTC and cache purge right after. I'll annotate runbook and tag customers (cc: product-ops).
Mike: Please add a blurb in incidents channel summarizing outage cause once done.
Rob: Backfill runbook snippet I'm adding to the DAG: 
```
# DAG: telemetry_backfill
params: {days: ['2026-03-15','2026-03-16'], mode: 'incremental', safe_mode: true}
```
Jess: Thanks team — schedule in calendar and I'll watch the canary. :thumbsup:
Anya: Closing thread; will follow up with postmortem link when written.
